newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM voices anger at nuclear accident coverup.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM voices anger at nuclear accident coverup.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Wednesday ordered raids on a state corporation in charge of reprocessing nuclear fuel after officials admitted falsifying a report about Japan's worst-ever nuclear accident.
"I am so angry (about the coverup) I cannot utter a single word," Hashimoto told reporters. "We will get third-party consultants to conduct a full probe."

As part of an all-out investigation ordered by Hashimoto, inspectors from the government's Science and Technology Agency on Wednesday raided the offices of the Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC).

They acted after PNC executives told a news conference late on Tuesday that they had falsified a report about a March 11 explosion at a nuclear waste processing plant, which exposed 37 workers to small doses of radiation.
The PNC has come under severe criticism for tardiness in alerting local officials to the accident, lax fire-fighting plans and outdated equipment.
The accident occurred at a PNC bituminisation plant, designed to harden low-level nuclear waste by mixing it with asphalt, at Tokaimura, on the Pacific coast 160 km (100 miles) northeast from Tokyo.
The official PNC report on the accident, issued on March 21, said staff at the plant visually confirmed that an initial fire at the plant had been put out.
The fire flared up again nine hours later, causing an explosion which released radiation into the atmosphere.

"In fact, no one had confirmed that the fire had been put out. The staff at the scene knew this but thought that there was no way to change the report once it was made official," PNC manager Hiromasa Nakano told Tuesday's news conference.

"I had believed that there were no lies (in the report) this time," PNC chairman Toshiyuki Kondo told the same news conference. "I deeply regret this. I thought we had learned a lesson at Monju. I am truly sorry for this."

Kondo was referring to a December 1995 accident at PNC's experimental fast-breeder reactor, Monju. Four PNC officials have been accused of falsifying a report and hiding videotapes of a massive coolant leak at Monju.
There was no radiation leak but the plant remains closed.
A Science and Technology Agency spokesman said the Tokaimura report was an official document which the PNC was required by law to submit to the government.
"False entries can lead to prosecution," the agency spokesman said.

The Tokaimura complex, Japan's only nuclear fuel reprocessing unit, recycles about 12 percent of the spent nuclear fuel from Japan's 50 operational commercial nuclear power plants, with the rest reprocessed at French plants.

Tokaimura is at the heart of Japan's long-term goal of supplying half of the country's power needs with nuclear power generation. At present, nuclear power plants supply one-third of the country's electricity.
